target_customer: Private credit funds, private equity firms and commercial banks
problem: Deal diligence, underwriting and portfolio monitoring rely on manual work over unstructured documents.
product_category: AI platform for private markets underwriting

founders.name: Don Muir
previous_startups: Arc, cash and capital markets platform (F2 was spun out of it in Sept 2025)
founders.background_notes: YC page says former private equity investor; the PE firm is not named on the YC page

founders.name: Emre Kazdagli
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder and CTO on f2.ai; background not opened

technical_complexity.rationale: Document-heavy financial analysis agents with security and compliance requirements; hard parts are accuracy and enterprise controls rather than research.

defensibility.rationale: Institutional deal history and workflows create lock-in once adopted, and named lender customers appear on the site; competing platforms exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Horizontal finance AI vendors target the same users per 2026 comparison pages; no acquisition or copy of F2 found.

market_need_then: Lenders and banks needed faster underwriting; F2 began inside Arc in late 2024 to serve lenders on its capital markets platform, per Arc's announcement.

branding.name_origin: Spun out of Arc, whose founders named the AI business F2; the reason for the name is not stated

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and concise, with short declarative headlines per the site

brand_strength.rationale: Short name but it collides with Formula 2 racing in search results; no brand press about F2 itself.

outcome_analysis: F2 spun out of Arc in September 2025 with a 10M round from Arc's existing investors and raised a further 14M in June 2026 led by HighlandX, for 24M in total equity per the company's release. It benefited from Arc's lender relationships and the founder's finance background, and shows named lender customers. The category has well funded rivals, so outcomes depend on enterprise adoption.
notes: Stage labels are 'other' because the press releases call both an equity round; an aggregator (Seedtable) calls them seed. Dealroom lists a 56M valuation for 2026, found only on one aggregator and not recorded. Rounds confirmed by the wire release plus AlleyWatch and the Arc announcement. Sources conflict on whether Emre Kazdagli is a co-founder (AlleyWatch and f2.ai say yes). One summary says Muir worked at Apollo and Onex; I did not open that source so it is not recorded. Competitor search returned only 2026 comparison pages, so the as-of-founding list is empty.
